title: Punjab Congress Infighting Deepens as Channi Threatens to Quit Over Warring's Leadership
excerpt: Former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi has warned he will resign as campaign committee chairman if Raja Warring stays on as Punjab Congress president, exposing deep fractures ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
body:
• Former Punjab CM Charanjit Singh Channi threatened to resign as campaign committee chairman if Raja Warring continues as state Congress president.
  • A survey by election strategist Sunil Kanugolu showed Congress support declining in Punjab's Malwa region after Warring's retention.
  • The Congress high command retained Warring despite an observers' report containing negative feedback, with 12 MLAs backing demands for his removal.
  • The power struggle is fundamentally a contest for the chief ministerial candidacy ahead of early 2027 state elections.

Leadership Crisis Erupts at Strategy Meeting

A strategy meeting convened by Congress general secretary KC Venugopal at party headquarters in late July ended without consensus after senior Punjab leaders clashed openly over the state unit's leadership. The session, intended to chart the party's course for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, instead laid bare a factional war that threatens to derail Congress's prospects in a state it desperately needs to win back from the ruling Aam Aadmi Party.

https://x.com/pradip103/status/2083483854585921904

Former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi, who currently serves as chairman of the Pradesh Congress Campaign Committee, delivered an ultimatum during the meeting: he would step down from his post if Amarinder Singh Raja Warring remained as Punjab Congress president. The declaration marked a sharp escalation from weeks of behind-the-scenes lobbying.

Senior leaders Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Rana Gurjeet Singh piled on, accusing the party leadership of ignoring ground survey reports and declaring they were unwilling to contest the 2027 elections under Warring's leadership. Venugopal reportedly reprimanded the dissenting leaders for airing the party's internal differences publicly.

Survey Data Fuels the Revolt

The confrontation intensified after election strategist Sunil Kanugolu presented survey findings indicating that Congress's support in Punjab's Malwa region — the state's largest electoral belt with over 60 of 117 Assembly seats — had declined following Warring's retention as state president on July 1.

"This isn't child's play."

— Bhupesh Baghel, AICC Punjab In-charge, dismissing calls for leadership change

The data contradicted the position of AICC Punjab in-charge Bhupesh Baghel, who had submitted a report to Venugopal recommending Warring's continuation. According to sources, Baghel's report noted that 25 of 29 district Congress presidents and four of seven Punjab MPs supported Warring. But the Channi faction pointed to the survey as evidence that organizational support had not translated into voter confidence.

A Battle for the Chief Minister's Chair

At its core, the infighting is a contest for Punjab's chief ministerial candidacy. In Congress's organizational tradition, the state president typically becomes the CM nominee if the party wins an election. By opposing Warring's presidency, the Channi camp is effectively challenging his claim to the top job.

Both Channi and Warring enjoy close relationships with former Congress president Rahul Gandhi, complicating the high command's ability to pick a side. Channi, who represents Jalandhar in the Lok Sabha, became Punjab's first Dalit Chief Minister in 2021 when he replaced Captain Amarinder Singh months before the 2022 elections. Warring, the Gidderbaha MLA, was Rahul Gandhi's handpicked choice to lead the Indian Youth Congress before ascending to the state presidency.

In mid-July, Channi took the unusual step of meeting Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa at his Chandigarh residence — a signal that the anti-Warring faction was consolidating across traditional rivalries within the party. He subsequently sought a direct meeting with Rahul Gandhi in Delhi, bypassing Baghel's mediation efforts entirely.

Baghel's Mediation Falls Short

Baghel spent six days in Chandigarh meeting party leaders in an attempt to broker peace, but the Channi camp set preconditions that undercut the exercise. They agreed to send only two representatives, refused to meet at the Congress Bhawan, and insisted Warring not be present.

Political analysts in Punjab described this as a calculated move. "If Channi personally goes to meet Baghel, it would be seen as a direct surrender, which would reduce his importance within the Congress," noted political commentator Pramod Batish. Another analyst, Pawandeep Sharma, warned that if Baghel left without resolving the factionalism, Congress would face renewed turmoil.

After the inconclusive Venugopal meeting, the atmosphere remained tense. Channi and Randhawa walked out while Baghel and Warring stayed for further discussions. Baghel said a follow-up meeting was scheduled because some key leaders had been absent.

Diaspora Stakes in Punjab's Political Future

Punjab's political direction carries particular weight for the global Punjabi diaspora — one of India's largest overseas communities, with significant populations in Canada, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Australia. Many diaspora families maintain deep financial, familial, and emotional ties to the state and closely watch its governance and electoral shifts. Congress's ability to mount a credible challenge to the AAP government of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann hinges on whether it can present a united leadership to voters. The current crisis suggests the party is far from achieving that unity, with early 2027 elections drawing closer.

What's Next

With no resolution in sight, the Congress high command faces a choice: back Warring and risk alienating a powerful faction led by a former Chief Minister with substantial Dalit voter support, or engineer a compromise that may satisfy neither camp. The party leadership is reportedly considering various options, but any decision is expected only after Channi secures his sought-after meeting with Rahul Gandhi. Until then, Punjab Congress remains a house divided — a vulnerability that both the AAP and the BJP will be eager to exploit as the state enters election season.
